faq.q: What's the difference between the Scale tab and the Crop Planner?
faq.a: Scale keeps the shape and just resizes: enter original width and height, then scale by percentage, target width or target height, and it preserves the ratio and estimates whether the file gets larger or smaller. Crop Planner compares a source size against a target ratio and tells you exactly how many pixels get cut (fill) or how much letterbox bar gets added (fit), with a keep/cut bar.

faq.q: Why did my 1920×1200 image not match a 16:9 slot?
faq.a: Because 1920×1200 is 16:10, not 16:9. The calculator simplifies any width and height to lowest terms using a GCD, so it exposes these near-identical-looking shapes. Enter the two dimensions and it shows the true simplified ratio, the decimal ratio and the megapixels, making it clear when a size will be letterboxed or cropped where 16:9 is expected.

faq.q: Which platform presets are built in?
faq.a: The Platform Presets section has exact-pixel sizes for YouTube (thumbnail, HD, 4K), Instagram (square, portrait, story, reel), Facebook, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, WhatsApp status and print sizes like 4×6, 5×7, 8×10 and A4 at 300 dpi. Clicking one fills width and height and derives the simplified ratio. There are also ratio chips like 16:9, 9:16, golden φ and cinema 2.39:1.

faq.q: Does it remember my dimensions and keep a history?
faq.a: Yes. Your last values across all three tabs are saved in your browser (ar_last) and restored on return, including which tab you were on. Finished sizes are kept in a history list of up to 12 entries (ar_hist), each labelled with its ratio, that you can click to reload. It also refuses negative or absurdly large values and rounds fractional pixels.
